scope: Build 32 NameSnap App Store listing asset quality only; 12 screenshots, 2 final 21-second previews and 2 selected 15-second posters.
firstUser: A host, teacher or streamer preparing a numbered group draw; needs fast setup, a clear selected person, repeat control and a visible result that can be announced confidently.
taskSubtype: Utilities / group name picker with numbered roster, Quick Pick, vertical Spin Wheel, no-repeat history and celebratory winner reveal.
independence: Reviewed rendered artifacts, current private category references and capture provenance. Did not read earlier critic scores or verdicts. Did not operate app UI, modify app code or assets, upload or submit.

categoryEvidence.audienceResonance: The winner-first 01 pair and large numbered result suit a host announcing a group draw. The celebratory treatment is more emphatic than a quiet classroom utility, but later input/history slides give practical evidence.
categoryEvidence.categoryRecognition: The blurred 02-05 slides retain a roster, selector, large draw control and result/history structure. The isolated 01 celebration is less self-explanatory without the surrounding set.
categoryEvidence.productSpecificity: The 04 vertical numbered picker and 05 numbered no-repeat history are specific to this product. The outer pill labels and device frames are familiar listing conventions.
categoryEvidence.primaryTaskClarity: 03 gives the gold SPIN control clear priority; 02 distinguishes the draft list and Add These Names to Pool. The iPad 03 action occupies less visual area than the phone equivalent.
categoryEvidence.visualHierarchy: 01 gives the number/name and next action clear prominence; 06 isolates the confirmation over a dimmed screen. In the iPad 01 celebration, background character artwork is partly behind the winner card and at the edge.
categoryEvidence.compositionDiversity: Input, draw, celebration, history and confirmation have different internal structures. iPad 03-06 reuse a wide app capture in the same portrait listing frame, so their outer silhouettes are repetitive.
categoryEvidence.contentRealism: 02 shows believable synthetic full names; phone 05 has winners 12/9/7 and 13 remaining from 16. The common 16-name sample is demonstrative content, not independently observed customer data.
categoryEvidence.domainArtifactFidelity: The actual numbered roster, picker, winner and reset dialog dominate the screen interiors. No generic chart or symbolic dashboard stands in for the draw; decorative celebration art still occupies significant space on 01.
categoryEvidence.crossScreenContinuity: Phone still 01 winner 7 Ava appears in still 05 history; 16 minus three shown winners equals 13. Each video preserves its own winner into history and 15 eligible entries. iPad still 05 uses a separate single-draw state, so the whole set is not one literal recording.
categoryEvidence.platformFidelity: Selected modes, toggle, close affordance, roster rows and confirmation remain within the displayed frames. Repaired phone reset frames have no partial preceding-card/status collision. Cropped marketing captures do not verify other app scroll positions or responsive states.
categoryEvidence.spatialEconomy: Phone frames fill their canvas with useful content. iPad 03-06 have a broad lower blank region between the wide app view and listing footer, reducing information density without clipping controls.
categoryEvidence.typography: Large black listing headlines and winner names survive gallery scale; list body text is legible at original size. Small iPad helper copy and the tiny celebration-variation line are less useful in a compact store gallery.
categoryEvidence.accessibility: Visible result identifiers, button text, selection geometry and pool checkmarks provide cues beyond color. The wheel deliberately fades off-center entries, and smaller iPad copy limits thumbnail readability. This score covers visual asset readability only; no VoiceOver, focus, Dynamic Type or reduced-motion behavior was tested.
categoryEvidence.interactionCredibility: Final preview samples show changing picker names, a SPINNING state, a settled winner and corresponding history; static 02 distinguishes draft names from an inactive draw. Preview input is already populated and the reset ends at confirmation, leaving those interactions unshown.
categoryEvidence.stateCompleteness: The advertised listing journey shows input, ready modes, spinning, success, recent winners and reset confirmation. It omits error, empty, exhaustion and a completed reset; these are outside this selected asset story and are not approved here.
categoryEvidence.distinctiveness: The numbered vertical picker and large name/number celebration distinguish NameSnap from all three circular-wheel references. Thick outlines and pastel gradients are common visual vocabulary rather than exclusive elements.
categoryEvidence.appStorePlausibility: The six concise promises per platform, real rendered app views and opaque target-size PNGs form a credible listing. iPad whitespace and a long winner hold in each preview are remaining editorial refinements.
categoryEvidence.implementationReadiness: Final files have exact dimensions, hashes and decodable media; capture provenance, viewport patch and rendering scripts are retained. This is a release-asset handoff of an implemented app, not a new UI specification; the generator was not independently rerun.
categoryEvidence.componentSemantics: Isolated winner, mode, wheel, history/pool and reset crops agree internally: number 7 repeats with Ava, wheel order wraps 16 to 1 to 2, history 12/9/7 yields 13 eligible, and Reset Pool explicitly retains names. Only a subset of the scrollable roster is visible.
categoryEvidence.materialFit: Gold actions, lavender depth and celebration imagery support a lively group draw while white rows preserve scanning. The iPad stills retain more decorative empty canvas than the phone set.

blurTest.evidence: Inspected release-review-samples/blur-diagnostic.jpg, made from all 12 originals. The list, selector, draw-control and winner hierarchy remain recognizable without reading small copy. The hero alone is more celebratory than utilitarian; the set resolves the task.

silhouetteTest.evidence: Compared both six-screen galleries and three private reference screenshots. Setup, winner, history and confirmation have distinct app interiors. No unrelated products were designed in this scope; consistent outer frames within one product are appropriate.

fiveSecondTest.evidence: Reviewer assessment, not a timed user study: 03 immediately prioritizes SPIN, 01 prioritizes a numbered winner, and 06 presents a named reset with two clear actions.

realityTest.evidence: Original-size 02-06 views contain realistic named rows, selected controls, counts and confirmation copy. Phone 05 count arithmetic is coherent; preview winner/history pairs match.

journeyTest.evidence: Each final video visibly moves from a populated input view through changing picker state to a specific numbered winner, matching history, and reset confirmation. Phone #8 Ethan Nguyen and iPad #16 Owen Lewis each leave 15 eligible. Static screenshots are separate fixtures, not one actual session.

platformTest.evidence: Both target sizes were inspected. No final key action or identifier is clipped. Fresh phone 18.5s and 20.5s reset samples show the repaired top crop and intact modal/actions. This does not establish appwide safe-area behavior.

buyerValueTest.evidence: Real list entries, actual changing picker footage, meaningful numbered outcomes and a visible no-repeat/reset workflow explain concrete buyer value; the deliverables are not wireframes or generic dashboards.

implementationTest.evidence: For this implemented-app asset release: exact original PNGs and decodable MP4s, target sizes, SHA-256 inventory, selected 15s poster equality, ASSET_REFRESH_2026-09-29.md provenance and retained capture/render scripts make the deliverable concrete. New application architecture, tokens and behavior are outside this asset-only pass.

componentSemanticTest.evidence: Inspected exact-pixel winner, draw-setup, wheel, history-pool and reset crops in release-review-samples plus all full-size screenshots. Name/number, selected mode, roster membership/count and reset semantics agree.

categoryReferenceTest.evidence: Compared Spin The Wheel - Random Picker, Tiny Decisions: Spin Wheel and Decide Now! Spin the Wheel current private reference snapshots, plus Utilities category guide. NameSnap preserves numbered-roster/vertical-picker semantics and does not trace their circular-wheel compositions. Device frames/captions remain outside the canonical UI.

nonblockingFindings.finding: Wide app capture leaves a substantial lower quiet region; small helper text has lower gallery-scale utility.
nonblockingFindings.recommendation: For a future listing iteration, tighten the wide-view framing or rebalance the footer gap while retaining truthful native UI.

nonblockingFindings.finding: The winner remains on screen for roughly ten seconds, with moving confetti but little task-state change.
nonblockingFindings.recommendation: A future editorial cut could shorten the hold after the identity is readable. Current 21-second videos remain coherent and show genuine motion.

repairs.issue: Pre-repair phone reset segment showed a partial prior card colliding with the status area.
repairs.verification: After rerender, independently decoded fresh final files; inspected phone 18.5s and 20.5s original frames and new temporal gallery. Top crop/aspect-fit padding removes the collision while reset copy, actions and corresponding history remain visible.

references.comparison: Shares a fast group-draw task and result emphasis. Its busy segmented-wheel/device presentation is not copied; NameSnap uses a numbered vertical picker and roster.
Concise action promise and dominant real selection object are useful conventions. NameSnap differs in roster maintenance, numbered winners and high-energy celebration.
Clear one-tap decision promise is category fluent. NameSnap does not copy the circular multicolor wheel or dark-blue listing direction.

limitations: Asset-quality approval is limited to the exact 12 PNGs, two final MP4s and two selected 15-second posters inventoried here; it is not appwide design, functional, accessibility, privacy or Apple-review approval.

Static fixture screenshots show appearance and data consistency, not successful real-world input, randomness, fairness or CRUD behavior. A 300-variation promotional count is visible but the entire celebration library was not audited in this pass.

Motion evidence is independent half-second decoding and sequential visual inspection with selected original-size frames plus full stream decoding; it is not real-time 30fps playback or a formal flicker/stutter test.

Preview input is already populated; endings show reset confirmation, not completed reset. Both audio tracks are intentionally silent. The visible musical celebration marketing is not demonstrated audibly by these videos.
Marketing crops avoid a documented main-screen scroll/status-area issue; this review does not claim that issue is repaired in the shipping app.
Legacy 5-second poster files and the app icon are outside the requested final asset scope. Apple upload slot acceptance remains to be verified by the submitting agent.
verdict: PASS (93.7/100) for the exact final listing assets inspected. No remaining critical visual or internal-data contradiction was found after the reset-segment repair. Nonblocking iPad composition and preview-pacing refinements remain. This verdict permits an asset-quality handoff only and does not certify the whole app or guarantee Apple acceptance.
